name: Music Theory
title: Arranger
blurb: A structured creative side-skill that keeps Arin's mind fresh during heavy study and trains the pattern recognition and systems thinking consulting work rewards.

chapters.title: Notation and rhythm
chapters.read: An introductory music-theory textbook's (or a free online theory course's) lessons on the staff, treble and bass clefs, note values, rests, dots and ties, time signatures and tempo markings.
chapters.produce: Transcribe the rhythm of a short melody you know (8 bars) onto staff paper or in free notation software, with correct time signature, beaming and bar lines.

quiz.q: In 4/4 time, how many eighth notes fill one bar?
quiz.ex: One quarter-note beat holds two eighths, and 4 beats × 2 = 8.

quiz.q: A dotted half note lasts how many quarter-note beats?
quiz.ex: Half note = 2 beats; the dot adds half its value (1), giving 3.

quiz.q: What does the time signature 6/8 usually mean?
opts: Two main beats per bar, each a dotted quarter divided into three eighths
Six main beats per bar, each a quarter note
Three beats per bar, each a half note
Eight beats per bar, each a sixth note
quiz.ex: 6/8 is compound duple: six eighth notes grouped 3 + 3, felt in two.

quiz.q: From bottom to top, the lines of the treble clef staff are…
quiz.ex: Lines are E G B D F ('Every Good Boy Does Fine'); the spaces spell F A C E.

quiz.q: At a tempo of 120 quarter-note beats per minute, how many seconds does one bar of 4/4 last?
quiz.ex: One beat = 60/120 = 0.5 s; 4 beats = 2 s.

quiz.q: What does a tie do?
opts: Tells the player to play two different pitches smoothly
Shortens a note to half its value
Joins two notes of the same pitch into one longer sound
Marks the start of a repeat
quiz.ex: A tie adds durations of same-pitch notes; a curved line over different pitches is a slur.

chapters.title: Scales and keys
chapters.read: A theory textbook's chapters on the major scale, the three forms of the minor scale, key signatures, the circle of fifths and relative/parallel keys.
chapters.produce: Write out all 12 major scales with their key signatures in circle-of-fifths order, and play or sing at least four of them.

quiz.q: What is the pattern of whole (W) and half (H) steps in a major scale?
opts: W H W W H W W
W W W H W W H
H W W W H W W
W W H W W W H
quiz.ex: For example C D E F G A B C: half steps fall between degrees 3–4 and 7–8.

quiz.q: How many sharps are in the key signature of E major?
quiz.ex: E major: F#, C#, G#, D#.

quiz.q: What is the relative minor of C major?
quiz.ex: Relative keys share a key signature; the relative minor starts on the 6th degree (A).

quiz.q: Which major key has two flats in its key signature?
quiz.ex: B♭ major has B♭ and E♭; F major has one flat and E♭ major three.

quiz.q: Which note does A harmonic minor contain that A natural minor does not?
quiz.ex: Harmonic minor raises the 7th degree, G → G#, to create a leading tone.

quiz.q: How many flats are in the key signature of E♭ major?
quiz.ex: E♭ major: B♭, E♭, A♭.

chapters.title: Intervals and their frequencies
chapters.read: A theory textbook's chapter on interval quality and size (major, minor, perfect, augmented, diminished, inversions), plus an introduction to equal temperament and frequency ratios (A4 = 440 Hz, ratio 2^(1/12) per semitone).
chapters.produce: Make an ear-training log: identify 50 intervals with a free interval-trainer app and record your accuracy, then build a table of the 12 equal-tempered frequencies from A4 to A5.

quiz.q: What interval is C up to G?
quiz.ex: C D E F G spans five letter names and 7 semitones: a perfect fifth.

quiz.q: How many semitones are in a major third?
quiz.ex: For example C to E: C–C#–D–D#–E is 4 semitones.

quiz.q: A4 is 440 Hz. What is the frequency of A5, one octave higher?
quiz.ex: An octave doubles the frequency: 440 × 2 = 880 Hz.

quiz.q: In 12-tone equal temperament with A4 = 440 Hz, what is the frequency of A#4, one semitone higher? (2 decimal places)
When a major third is inverted, it becomes a…
quiz.ex: Inversions add to 9 in number (3 + 6) and major becomes minor.

quiz.q: Using the just (pure) ratio 3:2, what is the frequency a perfect fifth above 220 Hz?

chapters.title: Chords and harmony
chapters.read: A theory textbook's chapters on triads (major, minor, diminished, augmented), seventh chords, inversions and the diatonic chords of a major key, with chord-symbol notation (C, Cm, Cdim, G7, Cmaj7).
chapters.produce: Spell and play all seven diatonic triads and seventh chords in C, G and F major, and label each with its Roman numeral and chord symbol.

quiz.q: Which notes make a C major triad?
quiz.ex: Major triad = root, major third, perfect fifth.

quiz.q: A minor triad is built from the root plus…
opts: A major third and a perfect fifth
A minor third and a diminished fifth
A minor third and a perfect fifth above the root
A major third and an augmented fifth
quiz.ex: Minor triads lower the third of the major triad; the fifth stays perfect.

quiz.q: Which of these is a diminished triad?
quiz.ex: B–D is a minor third and B–F a diminished fifth, so B D F is diminished.

quiz.q: What are the notes of G7 (a dominant seventh chord)?
quiz.ex: Dominant seventh = major triad + minor seventh; G B D plus F.

quiz.q: A C major chord with E in the bass (C/E) is in…
quiz.ex: Third in the bass = first inversion; fifth in the bass = second inversion.

quiz.q: In a major seventh chord such as Cmaj7, how many semitones lie between the root and the seventh?
quiz.ex: C to B is a major seventh = 11 semitones (one less than an octave).

chapters.title: Progressions and functional harmony
chapters.read: A theory textbook's chapters on harmonic function (tonic, predominant, dominant), cadences, common pop and jazz progressions (I–V–vi–IV, ii–V–I) and secondary dominants.
chapters.produce: Analyse the chords of three songs you like with Roman numerals and mark each cadence, then write your own 8-bar progression that uses at least one secondary dominant.

quiz.q: In a major key, which chord has dominant function?
quiz.ex: V (and vii°) create tension that wants to resolve to the tonic I.

quiz.q: In G major, which chords form the progression I–V–vi–IV?
quiz.ex: Degrees of G major: I = G, IV = C, V = D, vi = Em.

quiz.q: A phrase that ends on the V chord is called a…
quiz.ex: Ending on V sounds open, like a comma; V–I is authentic, IV–I plagal, V–vi deceptive.

quiz.q: What is a ii–V–I progression in C major using seventh chords?
quiz.ex: In C: ii = Dm7, V = G7, I = Cmaj7.

quiz.q: In G7 resolving to C, the tritone B–F typically resolves to…
quiz.ex: B (leading tone) rises to C and F falls to E, which is why V7–I sounds so final.

quiz.q: In C major, what chord is the secondary dominant V7/V?
quiz.ex: V of C is G; the dominant seventh of G is D7 (D F# A C).

chapters.title: Song form and arranging basics
chapters.read: A songwriting or arranging guide's chapters on common forms (verse–chorus, AABA, 12-bar blues), section roles (intro, pre-chorus, bridge, outro), instrument ranges, transposing instruments and basic voice leading.
chapters.produce: Make a section-by-section map of one song (timings, bars, which instruments enter or drop), then arrange a 16-bar piece for three parts (melody, chords, bass) using smooth voice leading.

quiz.q: In a 32-bar AABA song form, the B section is usually called the…
quiz.ex: AABA = two statements of A, a contrasting B (bridge), then A again.

quiz.q: A 12-bar blues is played in 4/4 at 96 quarter-note beats per minute. How many seconds does one 12-bar chorus last?
quiz.ex: 12 bars × 4 beats = 48 beats; 48 × 60/96 = 30 s.

quiz.q: What is the usual job of a pre-chorus?
opts: To build tension and lead from the verse into the chorus
To repeat the chorus lyrics exactly
To introduce the song before the first verse
quiz.ex: The pre-chorus raises energy so the chorus lands with impact.

quiz.q: Good voice leading between chords generally means…
opts: Moving every voice by large leaps
Having all voices move in parallel fifths
Keeping common tones and moving other voices by small steps
Doubling the leading tone in every chord
quiz.ex: Smooth, stepwise motion with retained common tones makes parts easy to sing and play.

quiz.q: A B♭ trumpet sounds a major second lower than written. To make it sound a concert C, the part should show…
quiz.ex: Written pitch is a major second above sounding pitch for B♭ instruments, so concert C is written D.

quiz.q: Which is a common arranging technique to give the final chorus more energy?
opts: Add instruments or harmonies, or move the melody up (e.g. a key change)
Remove the drums and bass entirely
quiz.ex: Thickening the texture, raising the register or modulating upward lifts the final chorus.

boss.q: In 12-tone equal temperament with A4 = 440 Hz, what is the frequency of E5, seven semitones above A4? (2 decimal places)
In A minor, using the harmonic minor scale, what is the V chord?
boss.ex: Raising G to G# turns v (Em) into a major V, giving a strong pull back to Am.

boss.q: A perfect fifth is inverted. How many semitones does the resulting interval contain?
boss.ex: Perfect fifth = 7 semitones; its inversion is a perfect fourth = 12 − 7 = 5.

boss.q: A piece has three sharps in the key signature, keeps raising E to E#, and ends on an F# minor chord. What key is it most likely in?
boss.ex: Three sharps = A major or F# minor; E# is the raised 7th of F# harmonic minor and the final chord confirms F# minor.

boss.q: In C major, how are the chords Am – F – C – G labelled in Roman numerals?
boss.ex: A minor = vi, F = IV, C = I, G = V in C major.

boss.q: A song in 6/8 has a tempo of 60 dotted-quarter beats per minute. How many seconds does one bar last?
boss.ex: 6/8 has 2 dotted-quarter beats per bar; each lasts 1 s at 60 bpm, so 2 s.

boss.q: Which chord symbol matches the notes F, A, C, E?
boss.ex: F major triad plus a major seventh (E) = Fmaj7; F7 would have E♭.

boss.q: A cadence that goes V – vi instead of the expected V – I is called…
boss.ex: The ear expects I; landing on vi 'deceives' it while sharing two common tones.

boss.q: Using the just ratio 5:4 for a major third, what is the frequency a major third above 440 Hz?
boss.ex: 440 × 5/4 = 550 Hz (slightly lower than the equal-tempered C#5 at about 554.37 Hz).

boss.q: A piece in C major modulates to its dominant key. Which accidental becomes standard in the new key?
boss.ex: The dominant of C is G major, whose key signature has one sharp, F#.
